structural: The requirement text sets no structural obligation. It names no library, algorithm, signature, type, field, or interface to delegate through. Each clause describes what the review prompt says and how the reviewer behaves:

- The reviewer treats the five listed kinds of change as mechanical: splitting a compound requirement, clarifying an obligation with clear intent, rewording where only one resolution is sensible, adding an `{example}`, and updating stale requirements.
- The reviewer makes those changes in the revised text and never phrases them as questions.
- The reviewer does not automatically convert prose to RFC keywords, and does not strengthen or weaken what the draft promises.

The prompt is a Markdown document. Any prompt wording that conveys this guidance would meet the text, whatever its section layout or phrasing. So no clause is a structural obligation, and the supplied root needs no `{impl}` reference for one.

The supplied root, `assets/skills/habeas-requirements/references/review-prompt.md`, is a single section, `section[Requirement group review]`. Its outline lists the subsections Two kinds of finding, Finding gaps, Criteria, Examples and Report. It is the artifact whose content the behavioral text describes. Whether its wording matches the text is a content and test-adequacy question. This assessment does not cover that question.

behavioral: The requirement says the review prompt lists five mechanical changes. It also says the reviewer makes them in the revised text and never phrases them as questions. A further sentence says the reviewer does not automatically convert prose or commented API declarations to RFC keywords, and does not strengthen or weaken what the draft promises.

`tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[the_review_prompt_lists_the_mechanical_changes]` extracts the prompt's `**Mechanical changes:**` section. It uses `review_prompt_between`, which panics if either marker is missing. It then uses `assert_text`, which asserts that each phrase appears.

It checks these items:
- Splitting a compound requirement: "Split a compound requirement".
- Clarifying a clear-intent obligation while preserving required, recommended or permitted status.
- Not automatically converting prose or commented API declarations to RFC keywords, and not strengthening or weakening promises.
- Fixing vague or inconsistent terms, or an ambiguity with one sensible reading.
- Adding an `{example}` that pins an obligation down.
- Updating other requirements a change makes stale.

It also asserts the "make them yourself in the revised text, and never phrase them as questions" instruction.

Every obligation is mapped to an assertion on the prompt text. The "never phrased as questions" clause is scoped to the mechanical section, which is where the requirement puts it. The requirement only constrains what the prompt text contains, so phrase assertions on the prompt are an adequate check. I found no unmarked relevant tests and no untested obligations.
